cases.exposure_context_quote: A 26-year-old previously healthy male presented to the emergency department 4½ h after attempting suicide by injecting approximately 10 mL of 24% paraquat dichloride intravenously into the dorsal metacarpal region of his left hand at home.
cases.agent: paraquat dichloride (24% solution, approximately 10 mL, intravenous)
cases.agent_quote: injecting approximately 10 mL of 24% paraquat dichloride intravenously into the dorsal metacarpal region of his left hand
cases.circumstance: suicide attempt by self-injection at home; engineering graduate employed in an IT company with no occupational access; no past psychiatric illness

symptoms.quote: Shortly after injection, the patient experienced two episodes of hematemesis, profuse sweating, giddiness, chills, restlessness, and generalized burning sensations.

symptoms.finding: diaphoresis, giddiness, chills, restlessness, generalized burning sensations
symptoms.quote: Shortly after injection, the patient experienced two episodes of hematemesis, profuse sweating, giddiness, chills, restlessness, and generalized burning sensations.

symptoms.finding: bradycardia (pulse 56/min), pedal edema, injection-site swelling and erythema
symptoms.quote: Physical examination revealed pedal edema, bradycardia without murmurs, and localized swelling and erythema at the injection site.
On the second hospital day, the patient developed dyspnea with tachypnea (RR 40/min), tachycardia (111 bpm), BP 110/90 mmHg, and SpO₂ 98%.

symptoms.finding: refractory hypotension and recurrent cardiac arrests
symptoms.quote: Despite ongoing CRRT, vasopressors, and corticosteroids, he developed recurrent episodes of bradycardia and cardiac arrest.

labs.name: WBC
labs.value: elevated (leukocytosis; value not given in text)
labs.quote: Initial blood investigations [Table 1] revealed an elevated WBC count suggestive of leukocytosis.

labs.name: serum creatinine
labs.value: about two-fold higher than the normal range
labs.quote: Serum creatinine was about two-fold higher than the normal range, suggested impaired kidney function.

labs.name: potassium and magnesium
labs.quote: Electrolyte analysis showed mild hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, as the levels of K+ and Mg²+ were slightly reduced.

labs.name: phosphate
labs.quote: Additionally, hyperphosphatemia (4.9 mg/dL) and hyperuricemia (7.1 mg/dL) were also observed.

labs.name: uric acid
labs.quote: Additionally, hyperphosphatemia (4.9 mg/dL) and hyperuricemia (7.1 mg/dL) were also observed.

labs.name: ABG (admission)
labs.value: pH 7.335, pCO2 26.2 mmHg, pO2 91.5 mmHg (metabolic acidosis)
labs.quote: Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis revealed metabolic acidosis (pH: 7.335, pCO2: 26.2 mmHg, pO2: 91.5 mmHg).

labs.name: ABG (day 2)
labs.quote: ABG revealed worsening metabolic acidosis (pH: 7.276, HCO₃⁻: 12.3 mmol/L, pO₂: 60.4 mmHg).

labs.name: urinalysis
labs.value: proteinuria, glycosuria, granular casts; specific gravity 1.015
labs.quote: The presence of granular casts in urine was an important abnormal finding that may have indicated renal parenchymal damage

treatment.name: Ryle's tube and Foley's catheter insertion
treatment.quote: after disclosure, a Ryle's tube and a Foley's catheter were inserted.

treatment.name: hemodialysis (initiated 7 h after exposure, 3 h)
treatment.quote: hemodialysis was initiated 7 h after exposure for 3 h.

treatment.name: continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT)
treatment.quote: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) was started later in the same clinical course.

treatment.name: intravenous ceftriaxone
treatment.quote: The patient received intravenous ceftriaxone, N-acetylcysteine (loading dose 12 g over 1 h, followed by sequential infusions), and pantoprazole.

treatment.name: N-acetylcysteine (loading 12 g over 1 h, then sequential infusions)
treatment.quote: N-acetylcysteine (loading dose 12 g over 1 h, followed by sequential infusions)

treatment.name: pantoprazole
treatment.quote: The patient received intravenous ceftriaxone, N-acetylcysteine (loading dose 12 g over 1 h, followed by sequential infusions), and pantoprazole.

treatment.name: vasopressors and corticosteroids
treatment.quote: Despite ongoing CRRT, vasopressors, and corticosteroids, he developed recurrent episodes of bradycardia and cardiac arrest.

cases.icu_admission: UNVERIFIED (intensive supportive care implied; explicit ICU admission not stated)
cases.outcome: died 28 h after admission after multiple cardiac arrests and refractory shock
cases.outcome_quote: After multiple cardiac arrests, he was pronounced dead 28 h after admission.
cases.notes: Patient initially concealed the mode of poisoning. Baseline chest radiography normal. Intravenous paraquat poisoning is rare and almost uniformly fatal.
